paragraphs.text: He prayeth once and again for audience; and would have God to hear him with both ears. Thus he prayed (saith the Greek title of this psalm) when his son Absalom was up in arms against him; and it may seem so, by the next words, De fuga ab Absolom (R. Obad. Gaon).

This is insignis sententia, siqua usquam in sacris literis extat (saith Beza), an excellent sentence as any is in all the Bible, saying the same that St Paul doth, Rom 3:24, that justification is by faith alone, and not by works. David would not be dealt with in strictness of justice. Lord, go not to law with me, so some render it; go not into the judgment hall, so the Chaldee. All St Paul’s care was, that when he was sought for by God’s justice, he might be found in Christ, not having his own righteoushess which is of the law, &c., Php 3:9. The best lamb should be slaughtered, except the ram had been sacrificed, that Isaac might be saved.
paragraphs.anchor: And enter not into judgment with thy servant

paragraphs.text: Woe to the life of man, saith an ancient, though never so commendable, if it should have judgment without mercy; if there be not an επιεικεια to moderate that ακριβοδικαιον, the severity of utmost right. We read of a certain Dutch divine, who being about to die, was full of fears and doubts. And when some said to him, You have been so active and faithful, why should you fear? Oh, said he, the judgment of man and the judgment of God are different. Sordet in conspectu Iudicis, &c.

Quasi rabie ferali percitus, he hath raged unreasonably. The utmost of a danger is to be related before the Lord in prayer, and to be acknowledged after we are delivered out of it, by way of thankfulness.
paragraphs.anchor: For the enemy hath persecuted my soul

paragraphs.text: God’s dearest children have their passions; against that stoic apathy. A sheep bitten by a dog is no less sensible of the pain thereof than a swine is; though he make not such an outcry.

Wherein I was delivered from the lion and the bear; yea, from the hand of all mine enemies, and from the hand of Saul, Psa 18:1, title. More than this, Saecula antiquitus praeterita recolo, I run over and ruminate all the ancient monuments of thy mercy to the patriarchs and others; since all that is written was "written for our instruction, that we through patience and comfort of the Scriptures might have hope," Rom 15:4. See Psa 77:4; Psa 77:6.
paragraphs.anchor: I remember the days of old

paragraphs.text: As a poor beggar for an alms. Beggary here is not the easiest and poorest trade, but the hardest and richest of all other.
paragraphs.anchor: I stretch forth my hands unto thee

paragraphs.text: And is therefore a fit subject for thy Spirit of grace and comfort to be poured upon, Isa 44:3; Isa 55:1.
A very pathetic prayer uttered in many words to like purpose; as the manner is, in extreme danger.

I am ready to sink and to swoon. This David knew; God hath a great care that the spirit fail not before him, and the souls which he hath made, Isa 57:16. When Bezoard stone is beaten we see that none of it be lost; not so when ordinary spices: so here, for ordinary spirits God cares not much what becometh of them, as he doth of the choice spirits of his people.

Cause me to hear … in the morning] Mane, id est mature, as soon as may be, or (at least) as is meet, make me to hear of joy and gladness, speak comfort to my conscience, and help to my afflicted condition.
Deliverance from enemies is a fruit of our friendship with God.
paragraphs.anchor: Deliver me, O Lord, from mine enemies

paragraphs.text: Orat nunc pro salute animae, ut ante pro corporis, saith Kimchi. Now he prayeth for his soul’s health; and would be as well delivered from his corruptions within as from his enemies without. Lord, save me from that naughty man myself, said an ancient.
paragraphs.anchor: Teach me to do thy will

paragraphs.text: The fruit of it is in all goodness, and righteousness, and truth, Eph 5:9, and it is the Spirit only that quickeneth, Joh 6:63, by purging out the dross that is in us, 1Pe 1:22, setting us to work, Eze 36:27, helping our infirmities, Rom 8:26; stirring us up to holy duties, partly by immediate motions, and partly by the ministry of the word made effectual, 1Pe 1:2 2Th 2:13. And, lastly, sanctifying the offering up both of ourselves and of our services to God, as the altar sanctifieth the gift, Rom 15:16. Cyril gathereth from this text, that the good Spirit is God, because none is good but God.
Or, on even ground, as Isa 26:7; Isa 26:10 Psa 26:12, or into the right land, i.e. heaven, Per viam planam et aequam.
Who am no better than a living carcass, a walking sepulchre of myself.
I can bring it in, but thou only canst bring it out.
paragraphs.anchor: Bring my soul out of trouble

paragraphs.text: Because not so much mine as thine; and those also implacable and irrecoverable. Elsewhere he saith, Slay them not, lest my people forget. {See Trapp on "Psa 59:11"}
